   107→def _prune_old_superseded(plan: PlanModel, now_dt: datetime) -> list[str]:
   108→    """Remove superseded entries older than TTL. Returns pruned IDs."""
   109→    superseded = plan.get("superseded", {})
   110→    cutoff = now_dt - timedelta(days=SUPERSEDED_TTL_DAYS)
   111→    to_prune: list[str] = []
   112→
   113→    for fid, entry in superseded.items():
   114→        ts = entry.get("superseded_at", "")
   115→        try:
   116→            entry_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)
   117→            if entry_dt.tzinfo is None:
   118→                entry_dt = entry_dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
   119→            if entry_dt < cutoff:
   120→                to_prune.append(fid)
   121→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   122→            to_prune.append(fid)
   123→
   124→    for fid in to_prune:
   125→        superseded.pop(fid, None)
   126→        # Also clean up stale overrides
   127→        plan.get("overrides", {}).pop(fid, None)
   128→
   129→    return to_prune
   130→
   131→
   132→def reconcile_plan_after_scan(
   133→    plan: PlanModel,
   134→    state: StateModel,
   135→) -> ReconcileResult:
   136→    """Reconcile plan against current state after a scan.
   137→
   138→    Finds IDs referenced in the plan that no longer exist or are no longer
   139→    open, moves them to superseded, and prunes old superseded entries.
   140→    """
   141→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   142→    result = ReconcileResult()
   143→    now = utc_now()
   144→    now_dt = datetime.now(UTC)
   145→
   146→    # Collect all issue IDs referenced by the plan
   147→    referenced_ids: set[str] = set()
   148→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   149→    referenced_ids.update(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   150→    for override_id in plan.get("overrides", {}):
   151→        referenced_ids.add(override_id)
   152→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   153→        referenced_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   154→
   155→    # Exclude already-superseded IDs and synthetic IDs (managed by stale_dimensions)
   156→    already_superseded = set(plan.get("superseded", {}).keys())
   157→    referenced_ids -= already_superseded
   158→    referenced_ids = {
   159→        fid for fid in referenced_ids
   160→        if not any(fid.startswith(prefix) for prefix in SYNTHETIC_PREFIXES)
   161→    }
   162→
   163→    # Check each referenced ID
   164→    for fid in sorted(referenced_ids):
   165→        if not _is_issue_alive(state, fid):
   166→            if _supersede_id(plan, state, fid, now):
   167→                result.superseded.append(fid)
   168→                result.changes += 1
   169→
   170→    # Reconcile epic clusters: remove dead issues, delete empty epics
   171→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   172→    epic_names_to_delete: list[str] = []
   173→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   174→        if not name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX):
   175→            continue
   176→        issue_ids = cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   177→        alive_ids = [fid for fid in issue_ids if _is_issue_alive(state, fid)]
   178→        if alive_ids != issue_ids:
   179→            cluster["issue_ids"] = alive_ids
   180→            result.changes += 1
   181→        if not alive_ids:
   182→            epic_names_to_delete.append(name)
   183→    for name in epic_names_to_delete:
   184→        clusters.pop(name, None)
   185→        result.changes += 1
   186→
   187→    # Resurface stale temporary skips
   188→    scan_count = state.get("scan_count", 0)
   189→    from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import resurface_stale_skips
   190→
   191→    resurfaced = resurface_stale_skips(plan, scan_count)
   192→    if resurfaced:
   193→        result.resurfaced = resurfaced
   194→        result.changes += len(resurfaced)
   195→
   196→    # Prune old superseded entries
   197→    pruned = _prune_old_superseded(plan, now_dt)
   198→    result.pruned = pruned
   199→    result.changes += len(pruned)
   200→
   201→    # Log reconciliation if any changes were made
   202→    if result.changes > 0:
   203→        from desloppify.engine._plan.operations import append_log_entry
   204→
   205→        append_log_entry(
   206→            plan,
   207→            "reconcile",
   208→            issue_ids=result.superseded,
   209→            actor="system",
   210→            detail={
   211→                "superseded_count": len(result.superseded),
   212→                "pruned_count": len(result.pruned),
   213→                "resurfaced_count": len(result.resurfaced),
   214→            },
   215→        )
   216→
   217→    return result
   218→

   223→

   226→    triage_injected: bool
   227→
   228→
   229→def sync_plan_after_review_import(
   230→    plan: PlanModel,
   231→    state: StateModel,
   232→) -> ReviewImportSyncResult | None:
   233→    """Sync plan queue after review import. Pure engine function — no I/O.
   234→
   235→    Appends new issue IDs to queue_order and injects triage stages
   236→    if needed. Returns None when there are no new issues to sync.
   237→    """
   238→    from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import (
   239→        compute_new_issue_ids,
   240→        sync_triage_needed,
   241→    )
   242→
   243→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   244→    new_ids = compute_new_issue_ids(plan, state)
   245→    if not new_ids:
   246→        return None
   247→
   248→    # Add new issue IDs to end of queue_order so they have position
   249→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   250→    existing = set(order)
   251→    added: list[str] = []
   252→    for fid in sorted(new_ids):
   253→        if fid not in existing:
   254→            order.append(fid)
   255→            added.append(fid)
   256→
   257→    # Inject triage stages if needed
   258→    triage_result = sync_triage_needed(plan, state)
   259→    triage_injected = bool(
   260→        triage_result and getattr(triage_result, "injected", False)
   261→    )
   262→
   263→    return ReviewImportSyncResult(
   264→        new_ids=new_ids,
   265→        added_to_queue=added,
   266→        triage_injected=triage_injected,
   267→    )

    37→def _extract_subtype(issue: dict) -> str | None:
    38→    """Extract the subtype/kind from a issue.
    39→
    40→    Checks detail.kind first, then falls back to parsing the issue ID
    41→    (format: ``detector::file::subtype`` or ``detector::file::symbol::subtype``).
    42→    """
    43→    detail = issue.get("detail") or {}
    44→    kind = detail.get("kind")
    45→    if kind:
    46→        return kind
    47→
    48→    # Parse from issue ID — third segment is often the subtype
    49→    fid = issue.get("id", "")
    50→    parts = fid.split("::")
    51→    if len(parts) >= 3:
    52→        # For IDs like smells::file.py::silent_except, the subtype is parts[2]
    53→        # For IDs like dict_keys::file.py::key::phantom_read, subtype is last part
    54→        candidate = parts[-1]
    55→        # Skip if it looks like a file path or symbol name (contains / or .)
    56→        if "/" not in candidate and "." not in candidate:
    57→            return candidate
    58→    return None
    59→
    60→

    94→                f"{ct['committed']} committed ({ct['total']} issues){pr_str}"
    95→            )
    96→
    97→
    98→def _cmd_plan_reset(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    99→    """Reset the plan to empty."""
   100→    plan = load_plan()
   101→    queue_len = len(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   102→    cluster_count = len(plan.get("clusters", {}))
   103→    reset_plan(plan)
   104→    append_log_entry(
   105→        plan, "reset", actor="user",
   106→        detail={"previous_queue_size": queue_len, "previous_cluster_count": cluster_count},
   107→    )
   108→    save_plan(plan)
   109→    print(colorize("  Plan reset to empty.", "green"))
   110→
   111→
   112→def cmd_plan(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   113→    """Dispatch plan subcommand or generate markdown output."""
   114→    plan_action = getattr(args, "plan_action", None)
   115→
   116→    if plan_action is None:
   117→        _cmd_plan_generate(args)
   118→        return
   119→
   120→    if plan_action == "show":
   121→        _cmd_plan_show(args)
   122→        return
   123→
   124→    if plan_action == "queue":
   125→        cmd_plan_queue(args)
   126→        return
   127→
   128→    if plan_action == "reset":
   129→        _cmd_plan_reset(args)
   130→        return
   131→
   132→    if plan_action == "reorder":
   133→        cmd_plan_reorder(args)
   134→        return
   135→
   136→    if plan_action in (
   137→        "describe", "note", "focus",
   138→        "skip", "unskip", "reopen", "resolve",
   139→    ):
   140→        dispatch = {
   141→            "describe": cmd_plan_describe,
   142→            "resolve": cmd_plan_resolve,
   143→            "note": cmd_plan_note,
   144→            "focus": cmd_plan_focus,
   145→            "skip": cmd_plan_skip,
   146→            "unskip": cmd_plan_unskip,
   147→            "reopen": cmd_plan_reopen,
   148→        }
   149→        dispatch[plan_action](args)
   150→        return
   151→
   152→    if plan_action == "cluster":
   153→        cmd_cluster_dispatch(args)
   154→        return
   155→
   156→    if plan_action == "triage":
   157→        from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage_handlers import cmd_plan_triage
   158→
   159→        cmd_plan_triage(args)
   160→        return
   161→
   162→    if plan_action == "commit-log":
   163→        from desloppify.app.commands.plan.commit_log_handlers import cmd_commit_log_dispatch
   164→
   165→        cmd_commit_log_dispatch(args)
   166→        return
   167→
   168→    print(f"Unknown plan action: {plan_action}")
   169→
   170→
   171→# Backwards-compatible alias
   172→cmd_plan_output = cmd_plan
   173→
   174→__all__ = ["cmd_plan", "cmd_plan_output"]
   175→

   119→def migrate_v5_to_v6(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   120→    """Migrate v5 → v6: unified queue system."""
   121→    from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import (
   122→        TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS,
   123→        WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID,
   124→    )
   125→
   126→    order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   127→
   128→    # Handle legacy synthesis::pending or triage::pending
   129→    for legacy_pending in ("synthesis::pending", "triage::pending"):
   130→        if legacy_pending in order:
   131→            idx = order.index(legacy_pending)
   132→            order.remove(legacy_pending)
   133→            meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", plan.get("epic_synthesis_meta", {}))
   134→            confirmed = set(meta.get("triage_stages", meta.get("synthesis_stages", {})).keys())
   135→            stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit")
   136→            to_inject = [
   137→                stage_id
   138→                for stage_id, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names)
   139→                if name not in confirmed and stage_id not in order
   140→            ]
   141→            for offset, stage_id in enumerate(to_inject):
   142→                order.insert(idx + offset, stage_id)
   143→            break
   144→
   145→    if plan.pop("pending_plan_gate", False):
   146→        if WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID not in order:
   147→            insert_at = 0
   148→            for idx, issue_id in enumerate(order):
   149→                if issue_id.startswith("triage::") or issue_id.startswith("synthesis::"):
   150→                    insert_at = idx + 1
   151→            order.insert(insert_at, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID)
   152→    else:
   153→        plan.pop("pending_plan_gate", None)
   154→
   155→
   156→def migrate_synthesis_to_triage(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   157→    """Migrate synthesis::* → triage::* naming throughout the plan.
   158→
   159→    - Renames ``synthesis::*`` IDs to ``triage::*`` in ``queue_order`` and ``skipped``
   160→    - Renames ``epic_synthesis_meta`` key to ``epic_triage_meta``
   161→    - Renames ``synthesis_stages`` to ``triage_stages`` inside that meta dict
   162→    - Renames ``synthesized_ids`` to ``triaged_ids`` inside that meta dict
   163→    - Renames ``synthesis_version`` to ``triage_version`` in cluster dicts
   164→    """
   165→    # Rename synthesis::* IDs in queue_order
   166→    order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   167→    for i, fid in enumerate(order):
   168→        if fid.startswith("synthesis::"):
   169→            order[i] = "triage::" + fid[len("synthesis::"):]
   170→
   171→    # Rename synthesis::* IDs in skipped
   172→    skipped: dict = plan.get("skipped", {})
   173→    synth_keys = [k for k in skipped if k.startswith("synthesis::")]
   174→    for old_key in synth_keys:
   175→        new_key = "triage::" + old_key[len("synthesis::"):]
   176→        entry = skipped.pop(old_key)
   177→        if isinstance(entry, dict):
   178→            entry["issue_id"] = new_key
   179→        skipped[new_key] = entry
   180→
   181→    # Rename epic_synthesis_meta → epic_triage_meta
   182→    if "epic_synthesis_meta" in plan:
   183→        meta = plan.pop("epic_synthesis_meta")
   184→        if isinstance(meta, dict):
   185→            # Rename synthesis_stages → triage_stages
   186→            if "synthesis_stages" in meta:
   187→                meta["triage_stages"] = meta.pop("synthesis_stages")
   188→            # Rename synthesized_ids → triaged_ids
   189→            if "synthesized_ids" in meta:
   190→                meta["triaged_ids"] = meta.pop("synthesized_ids")
   191→        plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   192→
   193→    # Rename synthesized_out → triaged_out skip kind
   194→    for entry in skipped.values():
   195→        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("kind") == "synthesized_out":
   196→            entry["kind"] = "triaged_out"
   197→
   198→    # Rename synthesis_version → triage_version in clusters
   199→    for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
   200→        if not isinstance(cluster, dict):
   201→            continue
   202→        if "synthesis_version" in cluster:
   203→            cluster["triage_version"] = cluster.pop("synthesis_version")
   204→
   205→

   207→    "ensure_container_types",

   211→    "migrate_v5_to_v6",

# Audit Report: Concern Generator and Plan Subsystem

## Issue 1: Concern Generator as Shadow Scoring Engine

### (A) Is it still a problem? YES, with a critical twist.

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/concerns.py`
**Lines:** 540 (exactly as claimed)

The file has 16 top-level functions organized into signal extraction, classification, summary building, evidence building, question building, and three generators (`_file_concerns`, `_cross_file_patterns`, `_systemic_smell_patterns`).

**The hardcoded thresholds (11 instances across 5 functions) are dead code.**

The concern generator reads `detail.get("signals", {})` at lines 107 and 130, expecting a nested dict like `{"max_params": 12, "max_nesting": 8}`. But real structural issues in the persisted state have a FLAT detail dict: `{"loc": 400, "complexity_score": 25, "complexity_signals": ["function with 8 params", "nesting depth 6"]}`. There is no `"signals"` key at all. I verified this against the live state file at `.desloppify/state-python.json`: zero structural issues contain a nested `signals` dict.

This means all 11 threshold checks are completely inert:

| Threshold | Location (line) | Functions |
|---|---|---|
| `max_params >= 8` | 132, 162, 193, 219, 259 | `_has_elevated_signals`, `_classify`, `_build_summary`, `_build_evidence`, `_build_question` |
| `max_nesting >= 6` | 134, 164, 190, 222, 265 | Same five functions |
| `loc >= 300` | 136 | `_has_elevated_signals` |

**These thresholds diverge from the detector thresholds even if they worked:**

| Signal | Concern generator | Python detector | Generic (tree-sitter) | Holistic review |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| params | >= 8 | > 7 (threshold=7) | threshold=7 | >= 5 (display) |
| nesting | >= 6 | > 4 (threshold=4) | threshold=4 | >= 4 (display) |
| loc | >= 300 | 300 (Python), 500 (others) | 500 | N/A |

Notably, `mechanical.py` (line 158-171) has a CORRECT fallback -- when `detail["signals"]` is absent, it falls back to `detail` itself. The concern generator lacks this fallback.

**But the concern generator still DOES work** via non-threshold paths. The `_file_concerns` function (line 307) flags files when:
- 2+ judgment detectors fire on the same file, OR
- A single detector has "elevated signals" (the broken threshold path), OR
- 1 judgment detector + 3 total mechanical issues

The first and third paths work correctly. Only the `_has_elevated_signals` path is broken, meaning single-detector files with high params/nesting/LOC are missed.

### (B) Detection Gap Analysis

The tool's own scan found this about `concerns.py`:

- `responsibility_cohesion::desloppify/engine/concerns.py` -- "16 top-level funcs across 2 disconnected clusters (15, 1)"

That's a mild cohesion finding. The tool does NOT have:
- **No "dead code path" detector** -- It cannot detect that a code path is unreachable due to a schema mismatch (the `detail["signals"]` key never existing). This would require data-flow analysis or runtime profiling.
- **No "constant divergence" detector** -- It has no way to detect that `>= 8` in one file should share a constant with `threshold=7` in another. This would need semantic understanding of intent.
- **No "schema contract" detector** -- The structural detector produces data in one shape; the concern generator reads it expecting another shape. Without typed interfaces or runtime assertions, this is invisible.

The subjective LLM review (`subjective_review::desloppify/engine/concerns.py::changed`) is pending re-review. A skilled reviewer COULD catch the schema mismatch, but it requires understanding the end-to-end data flow across multiple files.

### (C) How to fix

1. **Fix the signal extraction** -- In `_extract_signals` and `_has_elevated_signals`, change `detail.get("signals", {})` to fall back to `detail` itself (as `mechanical.py` already does), OR restructure the structural detector to produce a nested `signals` dict.

2. **Extract shared threshold constants** -- Create constants like `ELEVATED_PARAMS_THRESHOLD = 8`, `ELEVATED_NESTING_THRESHOLD = 6` in a shared location (possibly `engine/detectors/base.py` or `core/thresholds.py`) and reference them from both the concern generator and the detector signal configs.

3. **The 540 lines are justified** -- Despite the review's claim, the concern generator is NOT a "shadow scoring engine." It does not RE-score issues. It reads existing issues (already scored by real detectors), groups them per-file, and synthesizes cross-cutting questions for LLM evaluation. This is legitimate aggregation logic. The real problem is the broken data contract, not the module's existence.

## Issue 2: Plan Subsystem Scope

### (A) Is it still a problem? PARTIALLY -- the scope is large but mostly justified.

**Total plan subsystem code:** 8,547 lines across 34 source files (10.0% of the 85,340-line production codebase).

**The largest files are the hot spots:**

| File | Lines | Issues found by tool |

| `stale_dimensions.py` | 758 | structural, responsibility_cohesion, smells |

The tool found **44 open issues** across the plan subsystem and concern generator, including:
- 10 structural issues

### (B) Detection Gap Analysis

The tool IS detecting problems here at the file level. It correctly flags:
- `triage_handlers.py` as 1,748 LOC with complexity score 93 (structural)
- `operations.py` as having 23 top-level funcs across 16 disconnected clusters (responsibility_cohesion)
- Multiple files with high cyclomatic complexity

**What the tool CANNOT detect:**
- **Package-level scope creep** -- There is no "package complexity" or "subsystem scope" detector. The tool operates at file granularity. It sees 10 individual structural issues but cannot synthesize "this entire package is 8,547 lines spanning 34 files, which is 10% of the codebase -- is it proportionate to its value?"
- **Feature utilization analysis** -- The tool cannot detect that 3 of 4 skip kinds are unused, that 0 of 2,122 overrides have descriptions, that promoted_ids has never been used. This would require comparing schema features against actual data usage.
- **Unused feature/code path detection at the feature level** -- The `permanent` skip kind, `false_positive` skip kind, `remapped` superseded status, `promoted_ids`, and override `description`/`note` fields all have implementation code but zero real usage. The tool's orphaned-file detector works at import graph level, not at "is this code path ever triggered" level.

The concern generator DID fire 9 concerns on plan subsystem files (7 mixed_responsibilities, 2 design_concern), which is meaningful. The systemic pattern detector (`_cross_file_patterns`) could also flag that many plan files share the same detector combos.

### (C) How to fix

**For the legitimate concerns:**

1. **Split `triage_handlers.py`** (1,748 lines, 10 high-cyclomatic functions). The tool already flags this. It has already been partially decomposed into `triage/` subpackage but the main file remains huge.

2. **Split `stale_dimensions.py`** (758 lines, 4 disconnected clusters per cohesion detector).

3. **Prune unused features:**
   - `promoted_ids` -- never used, remove the field and its handling
   - Override `description` and `note` fields -- 0 of 2,122 have values. Either remove the fields or reconsider why they're never populated
   - `permanent` and `false_positive` skip kinds -- 0 entries. May be intentional future capacity, but the implementation code for their attestation requirements etc. is premature
   - `remapped` superseded status -- 0 entries. The candidate-finding logic exists but remapping never triggers
   - Commit tracking (233 lines) -- barely used (1 commit). Evaluate whether this feature pulls its weight

4. **Keep the schema migrations** -- Per the CLAUDE.md backward compatibility policy, data migration code must be preserved. The 6 migrations (214 lines) are required for data integrity.

**The "jira" critique is partially valid but overstated.** The plan subsystem has legitimate use cases: it's the mechanism by which scan results get prioritized, triaged, and tracked. The queue ordering, auto-clustering, skip/defer, and reconciliation are genuinely used. But at 8,547 lines (10% of the codebase), with several unused features and massive individual files, it has clearly accumulated scope beyond its core mission. The fix is surgical pruning of unused features and decomposition of the oversized files, not wholesale removal.

   343→def on_detector_registered(callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
   344→    """Register a callback invoked after register_detector(). No-arg."""
   345→    _on_register_callbacks.append(callback)

   348→def register_detector(meta: DetectorMeta) -> None:
   349→    """Register a detector at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""
   350→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   351→    DETECTORS[meta.name] = meta
   352→    if meta.name not in _DISPLAY_ORDER:
   353→        _DISPLAY_ORDER.append(meta.name)
   354→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = frozenset(
   355→        name for name, m in DETECTORS.items() if m.needs_judgment
   356→    )
   357→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   358→        cb()
   359→
   360→
   361→def reset_registered_detectors() -> None:
   362→    """Reset runtime-added detector registrations to built-in defaults."""
   363→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   364→    DETECTORS.clear()
   365→    DETECTORS.update(_BASE_DETECTORS)
   366→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.clear()
   367→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.extend(_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   368→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = _BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   369→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:

   392→def dimension_action_type(dim_name: str) -> str:
   393→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   394→    best = "manual"
   395→    best_pri = 99
   396→    for d in DETECTORS.values():
   397→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   398→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   399→            if pri < best_pri:
   400→                best_pri = pri
   401→                best = d.action_type
   402→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")
   403→

   405→def detector_tools() -> dict[str, dict]:
   406→    """Build detector tool metadata keyed by detector name."""
   407→    result = {}

   409→        entry: dict = {
   410→            "fixers": list(d.fixers),
   411→            "action_type": d.action_type,
   412→        }
   413→        if d.tool:

   415→        if d.guidance:
   416→            entry["guidance"] = d.guidance
   417→        result[name] = entry
   418→    return result

1→"""Shared data types for language-agnostic detectors."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     7→
     8→
     9→@dataclass
    10→class FunctionInfo:
    11→    """Extracted function/method info for cross-language analysis."""
    12→
    13→    name: str
    14→    file: str
    15→    line: int
    16→    end_line: int
    17→    loc: int
    18→    body: str
    19→    normalized: str = ""
    20→    body_hash: str = ""
    21→    params: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    22→    return_annotation: str | None = None
    23→
    24→
    25→@dataclass
    26→class ClassInfo:
    27→    """Extracted class/component info for cross-language analysis.
    28→
    29→    For OOP classes: methods/attributes/base_classes are populated directly.
    30→    For React components: metrics holds hook counts (context_hooks, use_effects, etc.).
    31→    """
    32→
    33→    name: str
    34→    file: str
    35→    line: int
    36→    loc: int
    37→    methods: list[FunctionInfo] = field(default_factory=list)
    38→    attributes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    39→    base_classes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    40→    metrics: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    41→
    42→
    43→@dataclass
    44→class ComplexitySignal:
    45→    """A complexity signal to detect in source files.
    46→
    47→    Either pattern-based (regex matched per line, counted) or compute-based
    48→    (custom function that analyzes content and returns count + label).
    49→    """
    50→
    51→    name: str
    52→    pattern: str | None = None  # regex (None = uses compute fn)
    53→    weight: int = 1
    54→    threshold: int = 0
    55→    compute: Callable | None = None  # (content, lines) -> (count, label) | None
    56→
    57→
    58→@dataclass
    59→class GodRule:
    60→    """A rule for detecting god classes/components.
    61→
    62→    The extract callable pulls a metric from ClassInfo; if it meets the threshold,
    63→    the rule fires and contributes to the "reasons" list.
    64→    """
    65→
    66→    name: str
    67→    description: str
    68→    extract: Callable  # (ClassInfo) -> int
    69→    threshold: int
    70→

    55→
    56→def phase_dupes(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
    57→    """Shared phase runner: detect duplicate functions via lang.extract_functions.
    58→
    59→    When a zone map is available, filters out functions from zone-excluded files
    60→    before the O(n^2) comparison to avoid test/config/generated false positives.
    61→    """
    62→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
    63→
    64→    # Filter out functions from zone-excluded files.
    65→    if lang.zone_map is not None:
    66→        before = len(functions)
    67→        functions = [
    68→            f
    69→            for f in functions
    70→            if lang.zone_map.get(getattr(f, "file", "")) not in EXCLUDED_ZONES
    71→        ]
    72→        excluded = before - len(functions)
    73→        if excluded:
    74→            log(f"         zones: {excluded} functions excluded (non-production)")
    75→
    76→    entries, total_functions = detect_duplicates(functions)
    77→    issues = make_dupe_issues(entries, log)
    78→    return issues, {"dupes": total_functions}
    79→
    80→
    81→def phase_boilerplate_duplication(
    82→    path: Path,
    83→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
    84→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
    85→    """Shared phase runner: detect repeated boilerplate code via jscpd."""
    86→    entries = detect_with_jscpd(path)
    87→    if entries is None:
    88→        return [], {}
    89→    entries = _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(entries, lang.zone_map)
    90→
    91→    issues: list[Issue] = []
    92→    for entry in entries:
    93→        locations = entry["locations"]
    94→        first = locations[0]
    95→        loc_preview = ", ".join(
    96→            f"{rel(item['file'])}:{item['line']}" for item in locations[:4]
    97→        )
    98→        if len(locations) > 4:
    99→            loc_preview += f", +{len(locations) - 4} more"
   100→        issues.append(
   101→            make_issue(
   102→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   103→                first["file"],
   104→                entry["id"],
   105→                tier=3,
   106→                confidence="medium",
   107→                summary=(
   108→                    f"Boilerplate block repeated across {entry['distinct_files']} files "
   109→                    f"(window {entry['window_size']} lines): {loc_preview}"
   110→                ),
   111→                detail={
   112→                    "distinct_files": entry["distinct_files"],
   113→                    "window_size": entry["window_size"],
   114→                    "locations": locations,
   115→                    "sample": entry["sample"],
   116→                },
   117→            )
   118→        )
   119→
   120→    if issues:
   121→        log(f"         boilerplate duplication: {len(issues)} clusters")
   122→    distinct_files = len({loc["file"] for e in entries for loc in e["locations"]})
   123→    return issues, {"boilerplate_duplication": distinct_files}
   124→
   125→
   126→def _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(entries: list[dict], zone_map) -> list[dict]:
   127→    """Keep only in-scope, zone-allowed boilerplate clusters.
   128→
   129→    jscpd can return files that are outside language discovery (artifacts/docs).
   130→    Restricting to known zone-map files prevents unknown paths from being treated
   131→    as production issues.
   132→    """
   133→    if zone_map is None:
   134→        return entries
   135→
   136→    known_files = set(zone_map.all_files())
   137→    filtered: list[dict] = []
   138→    skipped = 0
   139→    for entry in entries:
   140→        locations = entry.get("locations", [])
   141→        kept_locations = [
   142→            loc
   143→            for loc in locations
   144→            if loc.get("file") in known_files
   145→            and not should_skip_issue(
   146→                zone_map,
   147→                loc.get("file", ""),
   148→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   149→            )
   150→        ]
   151→        distinct_files = {loc["file"] for loc in kept_locations}
   152→        if len(distinct_files) < 2:
   153→            skipped += 1
   154→            continue
   155→
   156→        normalized = dict(entry)
   157→        normalized["locations"] = sorted(
   158→            kept_locations,
   159→            key=lambda item: (item.get("file", ""), item.get("line", 0)),
   160→        )
   161→        normalized["distinct_files"] = len(distinct_files)
   162→        filtered.append(normalized)
   163→
   164→    if skipped:
   165→        log(f"         zones: {skipped} boilerplate clusters excluded")
   166→    return filtered
   167→
   168→
   169→def find_external_test_files(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> set[str]:
   170→    """Find test files in standard locations outside the scanned path."""
   171→    extra = set()
   172→    path_root = path.resolve()
   173→    project_root = get_project_root()
   174→    test_dirs = lang.external_test_dirs or ["tests", "test"]
   175→    exts = tuple(lang.test_file_extensions or lang.extensions)
   176→    for test_dir in test_dirs:
   177→        d = project_root / test_dir
   178→        if not d.is_dir():
   179→            continue
   180→        if d.resolve().is_relative_to(path_root):
   181→            continue  # test_dir is inside scanned path, zone_map already has it
   182→        for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
   183→            for filename in files:
   184→                if any(filename.endswith(ext) for ext in exts):
   185→                    extra.add(os.path.join(root, filename))
   186→    return extra
   187→
   188→
   189→def _entries_to_issues(
   190→    detector: str,
   191→    entries: list[dict],
   192→    *,
   193→    default_name: str = "",
   194→    include_zone: bool = False,
   195→    zone_map=None,
   196→) -> list[Issue]:
   197→    """Convert detector entries to normalized issues."""
   198→    results: list[Issue] = []
   199→    for entry in entries:
   200→        issue = make_issue(
   201→            detector,
   202→            entry["file"],
   203→            entry.get("name", default_name),
   204→            tier=entry["tier"],
   205→            confidence=entry["confidence"],
   206→            summary=entry["summary"],
   207→            detail=entry.get("detail", {}),
   208→        )
   209→        if include_zone and zone_map is not None:
   210→            z = zone_map.get(entry["file"])
   211→            if z is not None:
   212→                issue["zone"] = z.value
   213→        results.append(issue)
   214→    return results

   217→def _log_phase_summary(label: str, results: list[Issue], potential: int, unit: str) -> None:
   218→    """Emit standardized shared-phase summary logging."""
   219→    if results:
   220→        log(f"         {label}: {len(results)} issues ({potential} {unit})")
   221→    else:
   222→        log(f"         {label}: clean ({potential} {unit})")
   223→
   224→
   225→def _coverage_to_dict(coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus) -> dict[str, object]:
   226→    return {
   227→        "detector": coverage.detector,
   228→        "status": coverage.status,
   229→        "confidence": round(coerce_confidence(coverage.confidence), 2),
   230→        "summary": coverage.summary,
   231→        "impact": coverage.impact,
   232→        "remediation": coverage.remediation,
   233→        "tool": coverage.tool,
   234→        "reason": coverage.reason,
   235→    }
   236→
   237→
   238→def _merge_detector_coverage(
   239→    existing: dict[str, object],
   240→    incoming: dict[str, object],
   241→) -> dict[str, object]:
   242→    merged = dict(existing)
   243→    merged["status"] = (
   244→        "reduced"
   245→        if str(existing.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   246→        or str(incoming.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   247→        else "full"
   248→    )
   249→    merged["confidence"] = round(
   250→        min(
   251→            coerce_confidence(existing.get("confidence")),
   252→            coerce_confidence(incoming.get("confidence")),
   253→        ),
   254→        2,
   255→    )
   256→
   257→    for key in ("summary", "impact", "remediation", "tool", "reason"):
   258→        current = str(merged.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   259→        update = str(incoming.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   260→        if update and not current:
   261→            merged[key] = update
   262→        elif update and current and update not in current:
   263→            merged[key] = f"{current} | {update}"
   264→    return merged
   265→
   266→
   267→def _record_detector_coverage(lang: LangRuntimeContract, coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus | None) -> None:
   268→    if coverage is None:
   269→        return
   270→    normalized = _coverage_to_dict(coverage)
   271→    detector = str(normalized.get("detector", "")).strip()
   272→    if not detector:
   273→        return
   274→    existing = lang.detector_coverage.get(detector)
   275→    if isinstance(existing, dict):
   276→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = _merge_detector_coverage(existing, normalized)
   277→    else:
   278→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = normalized
   279→

   281→def phase_security(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   282→    """Shared phase: detect security issues (cross-language + lang-specific)."""
   283→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   284→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   285→    entries, cross_lang_scanned = detect_security_issues(
   286→        files,
   287→        zone_map,
   288→        lang.name,
   289→        scan_root=path,
   290→    )
   291→    lang_scanned = 0
   292→
   293→    # Also call lang-specific security detectors.
   294→    lang_result = lang.detect_lang_security_detailed(files, zone_map)
   295→    lang_entries = lang_result.entries
   296→    lang_scanned = max(0, int(lang_result.files_scanned))
   297→    _record_detector_coverage(lang, lang_result.coverage)
   298→    entries.extend(lang_entries)
   299→
   300→    entries = filter_entries(zone_map, entries, "security")
   301→    potential = max(cross_lang_scanned, lang_scanned)
   302→
   303→    results = _entries_to_issues(
   304→        "security",
   305→        entries,
   306→        include_zone=True,
   307→        zone_map=zone_map,
   308→    )
   309→    _log_phase_summary("security", results, potential, "files scanned")
   310→
   311→    if "security" not in lang.detector_coverage:
   312→        lang.detector_coverage["security"] = {
   313→            "detector": "security",
   314→            "status": "full",
   315→            "confidence": 1.0,
   316→            "summary": "Security coverage complete for enabled detectors.",
   317→            "impact": "",
   318→            "remediation": "",
   319→            "tool": "",
   320→            "reason": "",
   321→        }
   322→
   323→    return results, {"security": potential}

   369→def phase_subjective_review(
   370→    path: Path,
   371→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   372→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   373→    """Shared phase: detect files missing subjective design review."""
   374→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   375→    max_age = lang.review_max_age_days
   376→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   377→    review_cache = lang.review_cache
   378→    if isinstance(review_cache, dict) and "files" in review_cache:
   379→        per_file_cache = review_cache.get("files", {})
   380→    else:
   381→        # Legacy format: flat dict of file entries with no "files" wrapper.
   382→        # Filter out known top-level structural keys so they aren't treated as
   383→        # file paths, then reconstruct the canonical shape preserving them.
   384→        _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = frozenset({"holistic"})
   385→        raw = review_cache if isinstance(review_cache, dict) else {}
   386→        per_file_cache = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k not in _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS}
   387→        review_cache = {"files": per_file_cache}
   388→        if "holistic" in raw:
   389→            review_cache["holistic"] = raw["holistic"]
   390→
   391→    entries, potential = detect_review_coverage(
   392→        files,
   393→        zone_map,

   399→        if isinstance(review_cache, dict)
   400→        else None,
   401→        holistic_total_files=len(files),

   403→
   404→    # Also check holistic review staleness.

   410→    entries.extend(holistic_entries)

   413→    _log_phase_summary("subjective review", results, potential, "reviewable files")

   418→def phase_signature(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   419→    """Shared phase runner: detect signature variance via lang.extract_functions.
   420→
   421→    Backend-agnostic — works with any extractor that returns FunctionInfo objects
   422→    (tree-sitter, regex, AST, etc.).  Returns empty results when the lang has no
   423→    function extractor.
   424→    """
   425→    from desloppify.engine.detectors.signature import detect_signature_variance
   426→
   427→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
   428→
   429→    issues: list[Issue] = []
   430→    potentials: dict[str, int] = {}
   431→
   432→    if not functions:
   433→        return issues, potentials
   434→
   435→    entries, _total = detect_signature_variance(functions, min_occurrences=3)
   436→    for e in entries:
   437→        issues.append(make_issue(
   438→            "signature", e["files"][0],
   439→            f"signature_variance::{e['name']}",
   440→            tier=3, confidence="medium",
   441→            summary=(
   442→                f"'{e['name']}' has {e['signature_count']} different signatures "
   443→                f"across {e['file_count']} files"
   444→            ),
   445→        ))
   446→    if entries:
   447→        potentials["signature"] = len(entries)
   448→        log(f"         signature variance: {len(entries)}")
   449→
   450→    return issues, potentials

   453→def run_structural_phase(
   454→    path: Path,
   455→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   456→    *,
   457→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   458→    log_fn,
   459→    min_loc: int = 40,
   460→    god_rules=None,
   461→    god_extractor_fn=None,
   462→) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   463→    """Run large/complexity/flat directory detectors for a language.
   464→
   465→    Optional ``god_rules`` + ``god_extractor_fn`` enable god-class detection:
   466→    when both are provided, ``god_extractor_fn(path)`` is called to extract
   467→    class info, then ``detect_gods()`` finds classes matching multiple rules.
   468→    """
   469→    structural: dict[str, dict] = {}
   470→
   471→    large_entries, file_count = detect_large_files(
   472→        path,
   473→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   474→        threshold=lang.large_threshold,
   475→    )
   476→    for entry in large_entries:
   477→        add_structural_signal(
   478→            structural,
   479→            entry["file"],
   480→            f"large ({entry['loc']} LOC)",
   481→            {"loc": entry["loc"]},
   482→        )
   483→
   484→    complexity_entries, _ = detect_complexity(
   485→        path,
   486→        signals=complexity_signals,
   487→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   488→        threshold=lang.complexity_threshold,
   489→        min_loc=min_loc,
   490→    )
   491→    for entry in complexity_entries:
   492→        add_structural_signal(
   493→            structural,
   494→            entry["file"],
   495→            f"complexity score {entry['score']}",
   496→            {"complexity_score": entry["score"], "complexity_signals": entry["signals"]},
   497→        )
   498→        lang.complexity_map[entry["file"]] = entry["score"]
   499→
   500→    if god_rules and god_extractor_fn:
   501→        from desloppify.engine.detectors.gods import detect_gods
   502→
   503→        god_entries, _ = detect_gods(god_extractor_fn(path), god_rules, min_reasons=2)
   504→        for entry in god_entries:
   505→            add_structural_signal(
   506→                structural, entry["file"], entry["signal_text"], entry["detail"],
   507→            )
   508→        if god_entries:
   509→            log_fn(f"         god classes: {len(god_entries)}")
   510→
   511→    results = merge_structural_signals(structural, log_fn)
   512→    flat_entries, analyzed_dir_count = detect_flat_dirs(path, file_finder=lang.file_finder)
   513→    for entry in flat_entries:
   514→        child_dir_count = int(entry.get("child_dir_count", 0))
   515→        combined_score = int(entry.get("combined_score", entry.get("file_count", 0)))
   516→        results.append(
   517→            make_issue(
   518→                "flat_dirs",
   519→                entry["directory"],
   520→                "",
   521→                tier=3,
   522→                confidence="medium",
   523→                summary=format_flat_dir_summary(entry),
   524→                detail={
   525→                    "file_count": entry["file_count"],
   526→                    "child_dir_count": child_dir_count,
   527→                    "combined_score": combined_score,
   528→                    "kind": entry.get("kind", "overload"),
   529→                    "parent_sibling_count": int(entry.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),
   530→                    "wrapper_item_count": int(entry.get("wrapper_item_count", 0)),
   531→                    "sparse_child_count": int(entry.get("sparse_child_count", 0)),
   532→                    "sparse_child_ratio": float(entry.get("sparse_child_ratio", 0.0)),
   533→                    "sparse_child_file_threshold": int(
   534→                        entry.get("sparse_child_file_threshold", 0)
   535→                    ),
   536→                },
   537→            )
   538→        )
   539→    if flat_entries:
   540→        log_fn(
   541→            f"         flat dirs: {len(flat_entries)} overloaded directories "
   542→            "(files/subdirs/combined)"
   543→        )
   544→
   545→    potentials = {
   546→        "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),
   547→        "flat_dirs": analyzed_dir_count,
   548→    }
   549→    return results, potentials
   550→
   551→
   552→def run_coupling_phase(
   553→    path: Path,
   554→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   555→    *,
   556→    build_dep_graph_fn,
   557→    log_fn,
   558→    post_process_fn=None,
   559→) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   560→    """Run single-use/cycles/orphaned detectors against a language dep graph.
   561→
   562→    Optional ``post_process_fn(issues, entries, lang)`` is called after
   563→    creating single-use and orphaned issues to allow per-language
   564→    adjustments (e.g. confidence gating based on corroboration signals).
   565→    """
   566→    graph = build_dep_graph_fn(path)
   567→    lang.dep_graph = graph
   568→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   569→    results: list[dict] = []
   570→
   571→    single_entries, single_candidates = detect_single_use_abstractions(
   572→        path,
   573→        graph,
   574→        barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   575→    )
   576→    single_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, single_entries, "single_use")
   577→    single_issues = make_single_use_issues(
   578→        single_entries, lang.get_area, stderr_fn=log_fn,
   579→    )
   580→    if post_process_fn:
   581→        post_process_fn(single_issues, single_entries, lang)
   582→    results.extend(single_issues)
   583→
   584→    cycle_entries, _ = detect_cycles(graph)
   585→    cycle_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, cycle_entries, "cycles", file_key="files")
   586→    results.extend(make_cycle_issues(cycle_entries, log_fn))
   587→
   588→    orphan_entries, total_graph_files = detect_orphaned_files(
   589→        path,
   590→        graph,
   591→        extensions=lang.extensions,
   592→        options=OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   593→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   594→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   595→        ),
   596→    )
   597→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   598→    orphan_issues = make_orphaned_issues(orphan_entries, log_fn)
   599→    if post_process_fn:
   600→        post_process_fn(orphan_issues, orphan_entries, lang)
   601→    results.extend(orphan_issues)
   602→
   603→    log_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} coupling/structural issues total")
   604→    potentials = {
   605→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zone_map, single_candidates),
   606→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   607→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   608→    }
   609→    return results, potentials
   610→
   611→
   612→def make_structural_coupling_phase_pair(
   613→    *,
   614→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   615→    build_dep_graph_fn,
   616→    log_fn,
   617→) -> tuple:
   618→    """Create default structural/coupling phase callables for a language.
   619→
   620→    This keeps language phase modules declarative by letting them provide only
   621→    their complexity signals and dependency-graph builder.
   622→    """
   623→
   624→    def phase_structural(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   625→        return run_structural_phase(
   626→            path,
   627→            lang,
   628→            complexity_signals=complexity_signals,
   629→            log_fn=log_fn,
   630→        )
   631→
   632→    def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   633→        return run_coupling_phase(
   634→            path,
   635→            lang,
   636→            build_dep_graph_fn=build_dep_graph_fn,
   637→            log_fn=log_fn,
   638→        )
   639→
   640→    return phase_structural, phase_coupling
   641→
   642→
   643→__all__ = [
   644→    "find_external_test_files",
   645→    "make_structural_coupling_phase_pair",
   646→    "phase_boilerplate_duplication",
   647→    "phase_dupes",
   648→    "phase_private_imports",
   649→    "phase_security",
   650→    "phase_signature",
   651→    "phase_subjective_review",
   652→    "phase_test_coverage",
   653→    "run_coupling_phase",
   654→    "run_structural_phase",
   655→]

1→"""God class/component detection via configurable rule-based analysis."""
     2→
     3→
     4→def detect_gods(classes, rules, min_reasons: int = 2) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
     5→    """Find god classes/components — entities with too many responsibilities."""
     6→    entries = []
     7→    for cls in classes:
     8→        reasons = []
     9→        for rule in rules:
    10→            value = rule.extract(cls)
    11→            if value >= rule.threshold:
    12→                reasons.append(f"{value} {rule.description}")
    13→
    14→        if len(reasons) >= min_reasons:
    15→            entries.append(
    16→                {
    17→                    "file": cls.file,
    18→                    "name": cls.name,
    19→                    "loc": cls.loc,
    20→                    "reasons": reasons,
    21→                    "signal_text": f"{cls.name} ({', '.join(reasons[:2])})",
    22→                    "detail": {**cls.metrics, "name": cls.name},
    23→                }
    24→            )
    25→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), len(classes)
    26→

    11→def is_py_facade(filepath: str) -> dict | None:
    12→    """Check if a Python file is a pure re-export facade."""
    13→    try:
    14→        content = Path(filepath).read_text()
    15→        tree = ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
    16→    except (OSError, SyntaxError, UnicodeDecodeError):

    18→
    19→    if not tree.body:
    20→        return None
    21→
    22→    imports_from: list[str] = []
    23→    for node in tree.body:
    24→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import | ast.ImportFrom):
    25→            if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
    26→                imports_from.append(node.module)
    27→            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
    28→                for alias in node.names:
    29→                    imports_from.append(alias.name)
    30→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(
    31→            node.value, ast.Constant | ast.JoinedStr
    32→        ):
    33→            continue
    34→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
    35→            if (
    36→                len(node.targets) == 1
    37→                and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name)
    38→                and node.targets[0].id == "__all__"
    39→            ):
    40→                continue
    41→            return None
    42→        else:
    43→            return None
    44→
    45→    if not imports_from:
    46→        return None
    47→
    48→    loc = len(content.splitlines())
    49→    return {"imports_from": imports_from, "loc": loc}

    51→
    52→def detect_reexport_facades(
    53→    graph: dict,
    54→    *,
    55→    max_importers: int = 2,
    56→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    57→    """Detect Python re-export facade files and directories."""
    58→    entries, total_checked = detect_reexport_facades_common(
    59→        graph,
    60→        is_facade_fn=is_py_facade,
    61→        max_importers=max_importers,
    62→    )
    63→
    64→    facade_files = {e["file"] for e in entries}
    65→    _detect_facade_directories(graph, facade_files, entries, max_importers)
    66→    return sorted(
    67→        entries, key=lambda e: (e["kind"], e["importers"], -e["loc"])
    68→    ), total_checked
    69→
    70→
    71→def _detect_facade_directories(
    72→    graph: dict,
    73→    facade_files: set[str],
    74→    entries: list[dict],
    75→    max_importers: int,
    76→):
    77→    """Detect Python package directories where all modules are facades."""
    78→    by_dir: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    79→    for filepath in graph:
    80→        parent = str(Path(filepath).parent)
    81→        by_dir.setdefault(parent, []).append(filepath)
    82→
    83→    for dirpath, files in by_dir.items():
    84→        init_file = str(Path(dirpath) / "__init__.py")
    85→        if init_file not in graph or init_file not in facade_files:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        non_init_files = [f for f in files if not f.endswith("__init__.py")]
    89→        if not non_init_files:
    90→            continue
    91→        if not all(f in facade_files for f in non_init_files):
    92→            continue
    93→
    94→        dir_importers = graph[init_file].get("importer_count", 0)
    95→        if dir_importers > max_importers:
    96→            continue
    97→
    98→        total_loc = sum(
    99→            len(Path(f).read_text().splitlines()) for f in files if Path(f).exists()
   100→        )
   101→
   102→        entries.append(
   103→            {
   104→                "file": dirpath,
   105→                "loc": total_loc,
   106→                "importers": dir_importers,
   107→                "imports_from": [],
   108→                "kind": "directory",
   109→                "file_count": len(files),
   110→            }
   111→        )

    16→# Mutable initializer values

    18→_MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES = {"set", "list", "dict", "defaultdict", "OrderedDict", "Counter"}

    20→# Mutating method names

    23→    "extend",

    35→def _is_mutable_init(value: ast.AST) -> bool:
    36→    """Check if an AST value is a mutable initializer ([], {}, set(), etc.)."""
    37→    if isinstance(value, _MUTABLE_INIT):
    38→        return True
    39→    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    40→        func = value.func
    41→        if isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id in _MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES:
    42→            return True
    43→        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in _MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES:
    44→            return True
    45→    if isinstance(value, ast.Constant) and value.value is None:
    46→        return True
    47→    return False
    48→
    49→
    50→def _is_upper_case(name: str) -> bool:
    51→    """Check if a name is UPPER_CASE (constant convention)."""
    52→    return bool(re.match(r"^_?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$", name))

    55→def _collect_module_level_mutables(tree: ast.Module) -> dict[str, int]:
    56→    """Collect module-level names initialized to mutable values.
    57→

    59→    """
    60→    mutables: dict[str, int] = {}
    61→    for stmt in tree.body:

    63→            for target in stmt.targets:
    64→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and _is_mutable_init(stmt.value):
    65→                    if not _is_upper_case(target.id):

    73→            if _is_upper_case(name):

    76→            if stmt.value is not None and _is_mutable_init(stmt.value):
    77→                mutables[name] = stmt.lineno

   100→def _find_mutations_in_functions(
   101→    tree: ast.Module, mutables: dict[str, int]
   102→) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
   103→    """Find functions that reassign or mutate module-level mutable names.
   104→
   105→    Returns {name: [line numbers where mutation occurs]}.
   106→
   107→    Bare assignments (name = x) and augmented assignments (name += x) only count
   108→    as mutations when the function has an explicit `global name` declaration —
   109→    without it, Python creates a local variable. Subscript assignments (name[k] = v)
   110→    and method calls (name.append(x)) don't need `global` because they operate on
   111→    the object reference, not rebind the name.
   112→    """
   113→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
   114→
   115→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   116→        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   117→            continue
   118→        # Skip if name is a parameter
   119→        param_names = {
   120→            a.arg for a in node.args.args + node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.kwonlyargs
   121→        }
   122→        # Collect names declared `global` in this function
   123→        global_names: set[str] = set()
   124→        for child in ast.walk(node):
   125→            if isinstance(child, ast.Global):
   126→                global_names.update(child.names)
   127→
   128→        for child in ast.walk(node):
   129→            if isinstance(child, ast.Assign):
   130→                for target in child.targets:
   131→                    # Bare name assignment: requires `global` to actually mutate
   132→                    if (
   133→                        isinstance(target, ast.Name)
   134→                        and target.id in mutables
   135→                        and target.id not in param_names
   136→                    ):
   137→                        if target.id in global_names:
   138→                            mutations.setdefault(target.id, []).append(child.lineno)
   139→                    # Subscript assignment (name[k] = v): operates on the object, no `global` needed
   140→                    elif isinstance(target, ast.Subscript) and isinstance(
   141→                        target.value, ast.Name
   142→                    ):
   143→                        if (
   144→                            target.value.id in mutables
   145→                            and target.value.id not in param_names
   146→                        ):
   147→                            mutations.setdefault(target.value.id, []).append(
   148→                                child.lineno
   149→                            )
   150→            # Augmented assignment (name += x): requires `global` to actually mutate
   151→            elif isinstance(child, ast.AugAssign):
   152→                if (
   153→                    isinstance(child.target, ast.Name)
   154→                    and child.target.id in mutables
   155→                    and child.target.id not in param_names
   156→                    and child.target.id in global_names
   157→                ):
   158→                    mutations.setdefault(child.target.id, []).append(child.lineno)
   159→            # Mutating method call: name.append(...) — no `global` needed
   160→            elif isinstance(child, ast.Call) and isinstance(child.func, ast.Attribute):
   161→                if (
   162→                    child.func.attr in _MUTATING_METHODS
   163→                    and isinstance(child.func.value, ast.Name)
   164→                    and child.func.value.id in mutables
   165→                    and child.func.value.id not in param_names
   166→                ):
   167→                    mutations.setdefault(child.func.value.id, []).append(child.lineno)
   168→
   169→    return mutations

   172→def _detect_in_module(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, entries: list[dict]):

   208→    """Detect ``from X import mutable_name`` that creates a stale binding.
   209→

   211→    that import the name directly get a stale copy.  They should import the
   212→    module and access the attribute at call time instead.

   214→    files = find_py_files(path)
   215→
   216→    for filepath in files:

   246→            # Check if any imported name is a mutated global in the source module
   247→            for source_module, names in mutated_names.items():

   249→                if not (

   262→                                "mutation_lines": [],
   263→                                "mutation_count": 0,
   264→                                "confidence": "high",
   265→                                "summary": (
   266→                                    f"'from {module} import {alias.name}' creates stale binding — "
   267→                                    f"'{alias.name}' is reassigned at runtime. Import the module instead."
   268→                                ),
   269→                            }
   270→                        )

   273→def detect_global_mutable_config(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   274→    """Detect module-level mutable state that gets modified from functions.
   275→
   276→    Also detects stale import bindings: other modules that `from X import name`

   280→    """
   281→    files = find_py_files(path)

   283→
   284→    # Phase 1: collect mutated globals per module
   285→    mutated_names: dict[str, set[str]] = {}  # {module_path: {name, ...}}
   286→

   308→                filepath,
   309→                exc,
   310→            )
   311→            continue
   312→
   313→        _detect_in_module(filepath, tree, entries)
   314→
   315→        # Track which modules have reassigned globals (need `global` keyword)
   316→        mutables = _collect_module_level_mutables(tree)
   317→        if mutables:

   319→            reassigned = set()
   320→            for node in ast.walk(tree):

   322→                    continue
   323→                global_names: set[str] = set()
   324→                for child in ast.walk(node):

1→"""Class extraction helpers for Python structural analysis."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.engine.detectors.base import ClassInfo, FunctionInfo
     9→from desloppify.core.discovery_api import find_py_files
    10→from desloppify.languages.python.extractors_shared import find_block_end, read_file
    11→
    12→
    13→def extract_py_classes(path: Path) -> list[ClassInfo]:
    14→    """Extract Python classes with method/attribute/base-class metrics (>=50 LOC)."""
    15→    results = []
    16→    for filepath in find_py_files(path):
    17→        content = read_file(filepath)
    18→        if content is None:
    19→            continue
    20→        results.extend(_extract_classes_from_file(filepath, content.splitlines()))
    21→    return results
    22→
    23→
    24→def _extract_classes_from_file(filepath: str, lines: list[str]) -> list[ClassInfo]:
    25→    """Extract ClassInfo objects from a single Python file."""
    26→    results = []
    27→    class_re = re.compile(r"^class\s+(\w+)\s*(?:\(([^)]*)\))?\s*:")
    28→
    29→    index = 0
    30→    while index < len(lines):
    31→        match = class_re.match(lines[index])
    32→        if not match:
    33→            index += 1
    34→            continue
    35→
    36→        class_name = match.group(1)
    37→        bases = match.group(2) or ""
    38→        class_start = index
    39→        class_indent = len(lines[index]) - len(lines[index].lstrip())
    40→        class_end = find_block_end(lines, index + 1, class_indent)
    41→        class_loc = class_end - class_start
    42→
    43→        if class_loc < 50:
    44→            index = class_end
    45→            continue
    46→
    47→        methods = _extract_methods(lines, class_start + 1, class_end)
    48→        attributes = _extract_init_attributes(lines, class_start, class_end)
    49→        base_list = (
    50→            [base.strip() for base in bases.split(",") if base.strip()] if bases else []
    51→        )
    52→        non_mixin_bases = [
    53→            base
    54→            for base in base_list
    55→            if not base.endswith("Mixin") and base not in ("object", "ABC")
    56→        ]
    57→
    58→        results.append(
    59→            ClassInfo(
    60→                name=class_name,
    61→                file=filepath,
    62→                line=class_start + 1,
    63→                loc=class_loc,
    64→                methods=methods,
    65→                attributes=attributes,
    66→                base_classes=non_mixin_bases,
    67→            )
    68→        )
    69→        index = class_end
    70→
    71→    return results
    72→
    73→
    74→def _extract_methods(lines: list[str], start: int, end: int) -> list[FunctionInfo]:
    75→    """Extract methods from a class body as FunctionInfo objects."""
    76→    methods = []
    77→    method_re = re.compile(r"^\s+(?:async\s+)?def\s+(\w+)")
    78→
    79→    index = start
    80→    while index < end:
    81→        match = method_re.match(lines[index])
    82→        if not match:
    83→            index += 1
    84→            continue
    85→
    86→        method_indent = len(lines[index]) - len(lines[index].lstrip())
    87→        method_start = index
    88→        block_end = find_block_end(lines, index + 1, method_indent, limit=end)
    89→        methods.append(
    90→            FunctionInfo(
    91→                name=match.group(1),
    92→                file="",
    93→                line=method_start + 1,
    94→                end_line=block_end,
    95→                loc=block_end - method_start,
    96→                body="",
    97→            )
    98→        )
    99→        index = block_end
   100→
   101→    return methods
   102→
   103→
   104→def _extract_init_attributes(
   105→    lines: list[str], class_start: int, class_end: int
   106→) -> list[str]:
   107→    """Extract self.x = ... attribute names from __init__."""
   108→    attrs = set()
   109→    in_init = False
   110→    init_indent = 0
   111→
   112→    for idx in range(class_start, class_end):
   113→        stripped = lines[idx].strip()
   114→        if re.match(r"def\s+__init__\s*\(", stripped):
   115→            in_init = True
   116→            init_indent = len(lines[idx]) - len(lines[idx].lstrip())
   117→            continue
   118→        if in_init:
   119→            if (
   120→                lines[idx].strip()
   121→                and len(lines[idx]) - len(lines[idx].lstrip()) <= init_indent
   122→            ):
   123→                in_init = False
   124→                continue
   125→            for attr_match in re.finditer(r"self\.(\w+)\s*=", lines[idx]):
   126→                attrs.add(attr_match.group(1))
   127→
   128→    return sorted(attrs)
   129→
   130→
   131→__all__ = ["extract_py_classes"]
   132→

     3→Concerns are ephemeral: computed on-demand from current state, never persisted.
     4→Only LLM-confirmed concerns become persistent Issue objects via review import.
     5→

    16→from typing import Any, Literal, TypedDict, cast

    21→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    22→class Concern:
